pr_title: Refactor formula, cask and Ruby source downloads to use shared code
pr_body:
This is significant refactor that makes formula resources (including bottles, source archives, resource archives and patches), cask downloads, formula Ruby source downloads (which previously was a resource), and cask Ruby source downloads all use a common `Downloadable` class.

It means everything that downloads should be more aligned, and easier to add new things to that system should it be necessary in the future.

This has a significant UX improvement for cask Ruby source downloads which previously had zero progress feedback and had no caching between brew runs.

The diff is large and this change probably took too long for most people (it was a fair bit of work while realistically being low priority) but here's an overview:
* Note the changes to `api/cask.rb` and `api/formula.rb` which have methods that download the Ruby source and load the file. They are effectively identical to each other beyond the usual formula & cask differences.
* `api/download.rb` shows how all that's on top of the `Downloadable` system is a nice constructor with nothing extra.
* Formulary no longer defines a resource - it now reads two parts of the JSON in the same way that we read the rest of it so there's nothing magic there anymore.
* `formula_installer` and `cask/installer` code to load the source is now a single line of code.
* `resource.rb` and `cask/download.rb` also use `Downloadable`
* There's a new `URL` class, though this is really only used internally to `Downloadable` and its subclasses at the moment.
* Checksum validation code duplication is no more.
* Cask source mirror code now uses existing mirror logic that formulae etc use.

Potential breaking change:
* `Resource#version=` has been removed (we had two setters before which seemed odd to me), but this API should be private AFAICT.

Closes #14746.
pr_comments:
> is there any code shared with DownloadStrategy here or is it just from Resource?

Yes everything here now uses DownloadStrategy - that was the key motivation to make everything that downloads actually use our main download system! That's how caching etc is implemented with no additional effort.

After this PR, the only thing that downloads and write a file to disk and doesn't really use this AFAIK is API JSON downloads, which we could also change if we want but I'm not going to touch that here and it's always going to be a bit special given we have logic in update.sh too. And SPDX updates are also not touched but that's a dev thing that's really not important at all or worth the extra complexity to write outside the cache.

> Yes everything here now uses DownloadStrategy - that was the key motivation to make everything that downloads actually use our main download system! That's how caching etc is implemented with no additional effort.

Very good 👏🏻. Just wasn't sure how these all fit together. Great work 😍 

> After this PR, the only thing that downloads and write a file to disk and doesn't really use this AFAIK is API JSON downloads, which we could also change if we want but I'm not going to touch that here and it's always going to be a bit special given we have logic in update.sh too.

Yeh, I think that's reasonable to keep fairly separate considering, as you said, it's in `update.sh` too and we're not doing checksumming.

> And SPDX updates are also not touched but that's a dev thing that's really not important at all or worth the extra complexity to write outside the cache.

Agreed.

I've moved the cached downloads from the base of `HOMEBREW_CACHE` to `HOMEBREW_CACHE/api-source`. I realised that this is more correct to do - we split formula and cask downloads already and cleanup.rb largely assumed the base of `HOMEBREW_CACHE` is formula related downloads so was not handling cleanup of source files correctly.

The git head is a part of the directory structure so it's trivial to tell when the cache is stale.

> there's even one unit test in a `downloadable_spec.rb` file I thought about this but basically `Downloadable` is not designed to be used directly. It's effectively an abstract class that should be subclassed in the places that need it: as we do with `Resource`, `Cask::Download` and `Homebrew::API::Download`. Coverage appears to be 95.95%. Not sure what the 4.05% is, because the file viewer is still broken (probably to do with the `Library/Homebrew` pathing):

issue_context.title: Unify formula and cask API source download handling
issue_context.body:
### Verification

- [X] This issue's title and/or description do not reference a single formula e.g. `brew install wget`. If they do, open an issue at https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/issues/new/choose instead.

### Provide a detailed description of the proposed feature

The formula way to handle downloads is fully fleshed out with progress information and the cask system is not. The stage where the download occurs is also different. It's worth consolidating the two.

### What is the motivation for the feature?

* Improved UX for cask source downloads
* More common shared code (better maintainability)

### How will the feature be relevant to at least 90% of Homebrew users?

The UX for cask source downloads is poor in that there is no progress information and it happens too regularly. Fixing that will provide a better experience.

### What alternatives to the feature have been considered?

Keep it separate and just modify the cask side for feature parity.
comments: I'm working on this right now (or rather once #14733 is merged), but it might take a day or two. Just opening this so there isn't duplicated work here.

I wonder if there'd be some way to cache the downloaded package source instead of re-downloading it every time. The fact that we're using the git revision makes that harder though. The reason I ask is that there are some commands where we really do need the source and fetching it infrequently doesn't seem like a terrible idea though it could end up being a lot of network requests. This was brought up as an option to add to the `brew cat` command (https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/issues/14815), for example, and there are a few developer commands that could work like that too in the future.

> I wonder if there'd be some way to cache the downloaded package source instead of re-downloading it every time.

Definitely could do this. Feels like it'd be a useful thing to add.

> The fact that we're using the git revision makes that harder though.

Indeed. Also want to make sure we cleanup these old versions sufficiently (although this could be done with the automatic formula/periodic `brew cleanup` runs).

Ideally it wouldn't but it can be due to the way that `url` may not be set immediately.

For resources: URL is defined later in a DSL in a `do block` but the nature of that means it may not actually be called and could be nil - we had various `url.nil?` checks already in `resource.rb` prior to this PR.
For cask downloads: we have a concept of lazily loaded URLs where the URL can only be calculated at install time. Plus casks allow basically anything to be nil at the moment.

I spent a fair bit of time fighting that but I can try again. Not sure yet but I can maybe do it by ditching the instance variable altogether and deferring a getter to subclasses, making this base class an abstract class.
